correctness.rationale: For every finite \(n\ge3\) and \(2\le k\le n-1\) with positive \(q_{ij}\), the killed generator equals exclusion minus diagonal collision intensity \(\kappa(S)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\subset S}w_{ij}\). Positivity makes labeled exclusion irreducible. A finite-state positive Perron eigenvector gives the Q-process; equality of off-diagonal rates implies eigenvector constant, hence constant \(\kappa\). Conversely constant \(\kappa\) gives the exact killed semigroup factorization and exponential survival law, and derivative at \(t=0\) proves the reverse. Swapping one site in each k-subset forces uniform symmetrized weights for \(2\le k\le n-2\); for \(k=n-1\) the missing-site identity reduces to equal degrees. Linear independence of degree-map rows gives the exact dimension. An explicit four-site counterexample and a marked independent-clock construction check the sharp exception. Standalone code passed 45 finite checks, including exact ranks and matrix Doob/semigroup tests; the analytic proof covers all finite \(n\) and continuous \(t\).

value.rationale: The all-generator criterion determines exactly when exponentially rare noncollision conditioning may be replaced by directly simulable exclusion. For every occupancy \(k\le n-2\), the symmetrized rates must be uniform; at \(k=n-1\) a high-dimensional cone of nonuniform regular rates becomes admissible, with a constructive four-site witness. The exact dimension and pair-mark conditional law expose an independent survival clock despite nontrivial collision partner dependence. This is a complete natural structural dichotomy and a motivated boundary for interacting particle laws, not just a computation of one example.
